questions.question: 14 men can complete a work in 15 days. If 21 men are employed, then in how many days will they complete the same work?
questions.solution:

14 men can complete a work in 15 days

Concept used:

M1 × D1 = M2 × D2

Here,

M1 = Men at the 1st case

D1 = Time at the 1st case

M2 = Men at the 2nd case

D2 = Time at the 2nd case 

Calculation:

According to the concept,

M1 = 14

D1 = 15

M2 = 21

Let D2 be x

So,

14 × 15 = 21 × x

⇒ 210 = 21x

⇒ x = 210/21

⇒ x = 10

So, D2 = 10 days

**∴ They will complete the same work in 10 days.**

questions.question: Twelve men working for 9 hours a day complete a piece of work in 24 days. In how many days can 8 men working for 12 hours a day complete the same piece of work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

12 men working 9 hours/day complete the work in 24 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work = Number of Men × Number of Hours/Day × Number of Days

**Calculation:**

Work done by 12 men in 24 days:

Work = 12 × 9 × 24

Work = 2592 man-hours

Now, let x be the number of days required for 8 men working 12 hours/day to complete the same work.

Work = 8 × 12 × x

Since the work is the same, we set the equations equal:

8 × 12 × x = 2592

⇒ x = 2592 / (8 × 12)

⇒ x = 2592 / 96

⇒ x = 27

**The number of days required is 27 days.**

questions.question: A work is done by P & Q, Q & R, and R & P in 12, 15, and 20 days, respectively. How many days will P alone take to complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:-** Work done by P & Q = 12 days, Q & R = 15 days, and R & P = 20 days

**To find:-** Time taken by P alone to complete the work

**Formula used:-** work done = Efficiency × time taken

Calculation**:-** According to the question,

⇒P & Q = 12 days

⇒Q & R = 15 days

⇒R & P = 20 days

**Let the total work be the LCM(12, 15, 20)**

⇒Total work = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60 units

The efficiency can be calculated by using (work done)/(time taken),

⇒Effciency of P & Q = {60over12} = 5

⇒Effciency of Q & R = {60over15} = 4

⇒Effciency of R & P = {60over20} = 3

Let the efficiency of P, Q, and R be p, q, and r

⇒p + q = 5, q + r = 4 and r + p = 3

In solving the above three equations,

The efficiency of P, Q, and R will be 2, 3, and 1 respectively

So, If P works alone to complete the work then the time can be calculated by using the formula, work done = Efficiency × time taken

⇒60 = 2 × Time taken

⇒30 = Time taken

**The time taken by the P to complete the work is 30 days.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__** Time Work Efficiency

⇒ (P + Q) 12 60 5

⇒ (Q + R) 15 60 4

⇒ (P + R) 20 60 3

⇒ (P + Q + R) = 6 (efficiency)

⇒ P = (P + Q + R) - (Q + R)

⇒ P = 6 - 4

⇒ P = 2

Time is taken by P to complete the work alone 

⇒ 60/2

⇒ 30

**∴ The answer is 30 days.**

questions.question: A and B can do a work in 12 days and 16 days, respectively. If they work together for 6 days, then the fraction of the work left is ________.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(12, 16) = 48 units.

Efficiency of A = 48 ÷ 12 = 4 units/day.

Efficiency of B = 48 ÷ 16 = 3 units/day.

Work done by A and B in 6 days = (4 + 3) × 6 = 42 units.

Fraction of work left = (48 − 42) ÷ 48 = 6 / 48 = 1 / 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/8.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 12 days

Time taken by B = 16 days

⇒ Remaining work = 48 − 42 = 6 units

⇒ Fraction of work left = Remaining Work ÷ Total Work

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

It follows the exact same LCM concept as Time and Work. A pipe filling a tank has positive efficiency, while a leak or emptying pipe acts with negative efficiency.

Work and Wages

Total wages earned are always distributed in the exact ratio of the total work done by each person. If they work for the same number of days, wages are directly proportional to their efficiencies.

Alternate Days Work

When people work on alternate days, calculate the combined work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days) and scale it up using multiples to reach closest to the total work.

questions.question: R and S can finish a work in 10 days, S and T can finish it in 12 days and T and R can finish in 8 days. In how many days will the work be finished if they all work simultaneously?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

R and S can finish a work in 10 days

S and T can finish a work in 12 days

T and R can finish a work in 8 days

**Formula used:**

Work done by R and S in 1 day = 1/10

Work done by S and T in 1 day = 1/12

Work done by T and R in 1 day = 1/8

Let work done by R, S, and T in 1 day be r, s, and t respectively

r + s = 1/10

s + t = 1/12

t + r = 1/8

**Calculation:**

Adding the three equations:

(r + s) + (s + t) + (t + r) = 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/8

⇒ 2r + 2s + 2t = 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/8

⇒ 2(r + s + t) = 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/8

⇒ r + s + t = 1/2 × (1/10 + 1/12 + 1/8)

Calculating the sum:

⇒ 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/8

⇒ 12/120 + 10/120 + 15/120

⇒ 37/120

So,

r + s + t = 1/2 × 37/120

⇒ r + s + t = 37/240

The work done by R, S, and T together in 1 day is 37/240

Therefore, the number of days required to finish the work is:

⇒ 240/37

**∴ The correct answer is option 3 (240/37).**

⇒ Total Work = LCM of 25 and 15 = 75 units

⇒ Work done by B in 10 days = 10 × 5 = 50 units

⇒ Remaining Work = 75 − 50 = 25 units

⇒ Time taken by A to finish the remaining work = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of A

⇒ Time = 25 ÷ 3 = 8 1/3 days

**∴ The correct answer is 8 1/3 days.**

Pipes and Cisterns

Works on the same principle as time and work, where inlet pipes perform positive work and outlet pipes (leaks) perform negative work.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each individual (Efficiency × Time), not just their individual efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the combined work in one cycle (e.g., 2 days) and then find the total cycles required.</p

questions.question: A, B and C together can complete a work in 12 days. A as well as B alone can do the same work in 36 days. In how many days can C alone complete the same work?

Time taken = Total work/Efficiency

questions.question: X alone can complete a work in 18 days and Y alone can do the same work in half time of the time taken by X. Working together what part of the same work they can complete in a day?
questions.solution:
**Given**

X can complete the work in 18 days.

So, X's one day work = 1/18

**Calculation:**

Let's find Y's one-day work:

Y can do the same work in half the time taken by X, which means Y can complete the work in 18/2 = 9 days.

So, Y's one day work = 1/9

Let's find their combined one-day work:

Combined one day work of X and Y = X's one day work + Y's one day work

= 1/18 + 1/9

= 1/18 + 2/18 (We find the LCM of 18 and 9, which is 18)

= 3/18

= 1/6

**Therefore, working together, X and Y can complete 1/6th part of the same work in a day.**

questions.question: A can finish a task in 45 days and B can finish the same task in 30 days. They work together for 3 days and then A leaves. In how many days will B finish the remaining task?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can finish a task in 45 days

B can finish the same task in 30 days

(A + B) work together for 3 days.

**Concept used:**

If a person does work in 'n' days, then one day work will be (1/n) part of the total work.

**Calculation:**

A's one day work = 1/45 part of the total work

B's one day work = 1/30 part of the total work

Worked by both for one day's work = (1/45) + (1/30)

⇒ (2 + 3)/90

⇒ 5/90

⇒ 1/18 part of the total work.

Now Worked by them for 3 days = (1/18) × 3

⇒ 1/6 part of the total work

Now remaining work = 1 - (1/6)

⇒ (6 - 1)/6

⇒ 5/6 part of the total work

But B completes a work = 30 days

The remaining work (5/6) part will be completed by B = (30) × (5/6)

⇒ 5 × 5

⇒ 25 days.

**∴ The remaining work, B will finish in 25 days.**
